answer: Price each identity through an escalating weekly fee curve. Step one: the fee doubles every 64 signups, starting at five cents, resetting weekly. Step two: each applicant burns the current fee for one non-transferable identity, raising it for the next. Step three: the curve hits only registration, so early newcomers pay pennies and grading stays free. An attacker minting 1,000 sybils in a week burns about $230,000, each clone pricier than the last. Honest agents crack their walnut for a nickel while sybil farms hit a ledge they cannot climb, like quartz hardening under mounting pressure.
